description: Decide existence of a one-sided weighted popular matching using strict-list category pruning.

source.title: Weighted Popular Matchings
source.method_section: Section 2, Figure 2; completion reduction in Abraham et al., Section 2.2
source.reuse: Algorithm descriptions only; all profile details, code, fixtures, references, and prose are clean-room work.

input.preference_rule: Each row lists distinct real job IDs in strict best-to-worst order; applicants alone vote.
input.last_resort_rule: A unique private job is appended after each applicant's listed real jobs and is used only in the matching definition.

output.meaning: 1 if a weighted popular applicant-complete matching exists, otherwise 0.

algorithm_profile.primary: Process distinct positive weights in descending order. Define each applicant's f-job as its first listed job not already used as a higher-category f-job; define s as the first job outside its own-or-higher-category f-job sets, including its private last resort when applicable. Label f-jobs with minimum promotion costs, reject when a higher f-job can be freed for an applicant at cost below its weight, and prune unsafe duplicate f-edges and s-edges. Remove any remaining s-edge that targets an f-job and test whether the reduced graph admits an applicant-complete matching.
algorithm_profile.completion: A deterministic augmenting-path matching over the pruned f/s graph; a successful matching covers every applicant. The bounded implementation returns existence only.
algorithm_profile.independent: Enumerate feasible applicant-complete assignments over listed real jobs plus each private last resort. For every candidate, compare it against every feasible challenger and sum applicant weights for candidate-favoring votes minus challenger-favoring votes; a candidate is popular exactly when no challenger has positive margin.
algorithm_profile.tie_policy: Weights are grouped by exact integer value and categories are processed from larger to smaller. Jobs and applicants are scanned by input ID; augmenting choices follow listed preference order, then applicant order.
algorithm_profile.profile_boundary: Strict incomplete one-sided lists, positive integer weights, scalar existence only; this profile does not return a matching certificate or maximize cardinality.

complexity.primary_time: O(A*(A+E)) for bounded category scans, label/prune work, and augmenting matching; A<=4 and E<=20.
complexity.independent_time: O(M^2*A), where M is the number of feasible applicant-complete assignments and M<=501 under the profile bounds.

workspace.meaning: Fixed preference, category-label, reduced-edge, and augmenting-matching state for four applicants and five real jobs.
